toolDescriptions.auto-subtitle: Generate accurate, time-coded subtitles from any video — as an SRT or VTT file, as a video with a switchable subtitle track, or as a video with the subtitles burned in for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

tool.subtitleOutputLabel: What do you want to get?

tool.subtitleMode_fileCost: 1 credit per started 5 minutes · up to 30 minutes
tool.subtitleMode_softDesc: An MP4 with a subtitle track viewers can turn on or off in players such as VLC or QuickTime.
tool.subtitleMode_softCost: 2 credits per started 5 minutes · up to 10 minutes
tool.subtitleMode_burnDesc: An MP4 with the subtitles drawn into the picture — always visible, even with the sound off.
tool.subtitleMode_burnCost: 3 credits per started 5 minutes · up to 10 minutes

t.faq.cost.a.subtitle: It is billed by length rather than per file, per started 5 minutes of video: 1 credit for the subtitle file only, 2 credits for a video with switchable subtitles and 3 credits for a video with burned-in subtitles, because those last two have to be processed again as video. There is no subscription: credits are bought in small prepaid packs, they never expire, and a conversion that fails never costs you anything.
t.faq.time.suffix.subtitle: Videos can be up to 500 MB — up to 30 minutes for the subtitle file and up to 10 minutes for video with subtitles.

t.intro.lead.subtitle: The subtitle generator transcribes the speech in a video and writes it out with timecodes. You get either a standard subtitle file, or the finished video itself — with a subtitle track viewers can switch on and off, or with the subtitles burned into the picture so they show everywhere.
t.steps.subtitle.1: Upload the video you want captioned — MP4, MOV, M4V, 3GP or WebM, up to 500 MB.
t.steps.subtitle.2: Choose the output — subtitle file, video with switchable subtitles or video with burned-in subtitles — and set the spoken language if you know it. The price is shown before you convert.
t.steps.subtitle.3: Click Convert and download the subtitle file or the finished MP4.
t.shapeFaq.subtitle.a1: Clear speech transcribes very accurately, including across accents. Background music, crosstalk and specialised terminology are where errors creep in, and setting the spoken language rather than auto-detecting it helps. If every word has to be perfect, choose the subtitle file first: it is plain text, so fixing the occasional word takes seconds in any text editor.
t.shapeFaq.subtitle.q2: Should I choose switchable or burned-in subtitles?
t.shapeFaq.subtitle.a2: Burned-in subtitles are part of the picture, so they show everywhere — the right choice for TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, where most people watch without sound and switchable tracks are ignored. Switchable subtitles stay a separate track that viewers turn on or off in players such as VLC or QuickTime; for YouTube itself, upload the subtitle file instead. If you need SRT or VTT, SRT works almost everywhere, while VTT is the format for HTML5 players on websites.
